chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and al-Washa' together, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I had a guest with me, so he desired to eat a citron with honey, so I fed it to him and ate with him. Then I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and there was a meal spread before him. He said to me, 'Approach and eat.' I said, 'I have eaten before coming to you a citron with honey, and I still feel its heaviness because I ate a lot of it.' He said, 'O servant, go to the maid and tell her to send us a piece of dry bread from what she dries in the oven.' So it was brought to him, and he said to me, 'Eat from this dry bread, for it digests the citron.' So I ate it. Then I stood up, and it was as if I had not eaten anything.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam recommend to digest the heaviness of eating citron with honey?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating the principle of using specific foods to counteract the heaviness or 'thiqal' of others, a concept rooted in humoral theory. It underscores the Imam’s attention to daily physiological well-being, demonstrating that spiritual guidance often encompasses tangible, health-oriented advice for the community. The narrative serves as a testament to the holistic nature of Shia teachings, where physical comfort is seen as conducive to spiritual presence.
